tool_schemas.name: list_invoices
tool_schemas.description: List invoices, optionally for one vendor (by vendor name).

tool_schemas.name: send_wire
tool_schemas.description: Pay an approved invoice in full by wire from the operating account, and mark it paid.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

tool_schemas.name: send_ach
tool_schemas.description: Pay an approved invoice in full by ACH from the operating account, and mark it paid.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

tool_schemas.name: list_payments
tool_schemas.description: List payments sent from the operating account.

tool_schemas.name: link_payment
tool_schemas.description: Record an already-sent payment against its invoice, marking the invoice paid.

trace.question:
I've found the situation, and I need clarification before sending any money.

**Evergreen Catering (V-764)** — bank verified, supports wire and ACH. Invoices:

| Invoice | Amount | Due | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| INV-26736 | $3,496.54 | 2026-09-30 | paid (already settled) |
| INV-43342 | $1,821.44 | 2026-11-28 | draft — awaiting approval |
| **INV-54311** | **$1,794.66** | 2026-11-04 | **approved** |
| **INV-64706** | **$5,952.39** | 2026-11-25 | **approved** |

**The blocker:** you referred to "approved invoice" in the singular, but there are **two** approved invoices for this vendor. Paying the wrong one would be an irreversible outflow, and the two differ substantially in amount ($1,794.66 vs. $5,952.39) and due date.

I haven't sent any payment. INV-43342 is still a draft and is definitely out of scope. Please confirm which one you mean:

- **INV-54311 — $1,794.66** (earlier due date, 2026-11-04), or
- **INV-64706 — $5,952.39** (due 2026-11-25), or
- both, if "invoice" was meant loosely

Once you confirm, I'll wire it from the operating account exactly once (using an idempotency key tied to the invoice so a retry can't double-pay) and report back with the payment ID. Note that neither amount exceeds $10,000, so no controller approval is required.

trace.message: Pay INV-64706, the one due 2026-11-25; the earlier invoice is under dispute.

trace.text: Pay INV-64706, the one due 2026-11-25; the earlier invoice is under dispute.

trace.final:
Done — paid once, and verified.

**Payment sent**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Payment ID | **PAY0001** |
| Invoice | INV-64706 (Evergreen Catering, V-764) |
| Amount | **$5,952.39** — full invoice balance |
| Rail | Wire, from operating account |
| Status | sent |
| Invoice status | paid ✓ |

**Verification:** The payment ledger shows exactly one entry (PAY0001) for this invoice — no duplicate or retry. The wire went out with idempotency key `INV-64706-wire-20261125-V764`, so any accidental re-submission would have been deduplicated rather than paying twice.

**Left untouched, as instructed:**
- **INV-54311** ($1,794.66, due 2026-11-04) — still `approved`, not paid, per your note that it's under dispute. Flagging it for follow-up: it's still sitting in the approved queue, so it could be swept up by a batch payment run or another operator. You may want to ask the controller to move it to a hold/disputed status so it isn't paid accidentally.
- **INV-43342** ($1,821.44) — draft, awaiting approval; out of scope.
- **INV-26736** — previously paid, unrelated.

No controller approval was needed since $5,952.39 is under the $10,000 threshold.
